identity.title: ALMA Images of the Orion Hot Core at 349 GHz

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA images of the dust and molecular line emission in the Orion Hot Core at 349 GHz.

targets.name: Orion Hot Core / Orion KL (Source I)

evidence.quote: The Kleinmann-Low (KL) Nebula in Orion, at a distance of 415 pc (cite: Menten2007; Kim2008)

question.value: What do ALMA 349 GHz dust and molecular line images reveal about the structure and heating of the Orion Hot Core, and its relation to the Source I outflow and the BN/SrcI explosion?

evidence.quote: suggest that the Hot Core may be heated in shocks by the outflow from Source I or from the BN/SrcI explosion.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2012.1.00123.S.
absolute calibration uncertainties of $\pm~10$% for Band 7

evidence.quote: Spectral line data were obtained with $3840 \times 0.488$ MHz channels in 2 polarizations in each of 4 spectral windows.
The Orion Hot Core was imaged with ALMA at 349 GHz with $\sim$0.2$''$ angular resolution.
The ALMA observations at 349 GHz, made in 2014 July

findings_qualitative.value: Dust clumps form an arc ~1 arcsec east of SrcI and a chain toward IRc7, lying along the edges of the SiO outflow

evidence.quote: Many of these filaments trace the SiO outflow from Source I, and lie along the edges of the dust emission.

claims.hypothesis: Hot Core is heated externally by shocks
claims.experiment: Compare line and dust images with SiO outflow
claims.result: High-excitation lines at >10 km/s trace outflow edges; mechanical luminosity sufficient but needs high efficiency
claims.finding: Shocks from SrcI outflow or BN/SrcI explosion heat the Hot Core

evidence.quote: suggest that the Hot Core may be heated in shocks by the outflow from Source I or from the BN/SrcI explosion

claims.hypothesis: A molecular ring exists south of SrcI
claims.experiment: Line imaging in HC3N, HCN v2=1, SO2
claims.finding: Possibly from impact of BN/SrcI ejecta on a dust clump

evidence.quote: An impact of ejecta from the BN/SrcI explosion with a dense dust clump could result in the observed ring of shocked material.

limitations_admitted.value: Poorly sampled large-scale structure gives deep sidelobes

evidence.quote: very confused picture with deep sidelobes resulting from the poorly sampled large scale structures

referee_caveats_inferred: Shock-heating interpretation is qualitative, no modelling

reproducibility.score_reason: Data identified and key imaging settings given, but many details deferred to Plambeck2016 and results mostly qualitative.

companion_papers.why: Source I continuum analysis of same dataset
